one_month_reasoning: No Oracle earnings in the window: Q1 FY27 was reported 2026-09-10 and Q2 FY27 should come around the second week of December, after 2026-11-04. Events inside the window are second-order but matter for an AI-infrastructure proxy with 56% realized vol. (1) Big-4 hyperscaler Q3 results in late October bring the first numeric 2027 capex guides. The standing capex view (base Big-4 2027 ~$1.08T, guides only went up in 2026) leans mildly positive for AI-capacity demand. (2) Any OpenAI financing or IPO-timing news. OpenAI is the largest RPO counterparty and drove the April selloff (CNBC 2026-04-28). (3) Credit-market signals on Oracle-linked project debt; the $18B New Mexico landlord loan was quoted at 89-91c on 2026-09-18. (4) Oracle's own fall AI World event, if held in October as usual. These cut both ways, and there is no clean post-earnings drift signal: the stock fell after a beat-and-raise quarter that came with a $20B ATM equity sale. So I keep a near-symmetric lognormal centred at ~$144 (tiny positive drift) with monthly sigma 0.16 (56%/3.5).

fair_value.method: Blend, at 2027-10-05, of P/E (0.45 weight: NTM non-GAAP EPS $11.0 x 15x = $165), sum of the parts (0.35: legacy software at 15x after-tax earnings plus OCI at 3.2x NTM EV/sales, less ~$170B net debt incl. finance leases, on 3.15B diluted shares = $120) and EV/EBITDA (0.20: haircut NTM EBITDA $77B x 10x, less $170B net debt, on 3.15B shares = $190). Blended = $154.

ORCL trades at 14.6x CY2027 consensus today.

bear.story: OpenAI (largest RPO counterparty) slows, renegotiates or defers. RPO conversion slips, and the 13% recognised within 12 months misses. Oracle keeps paying $90-95B gross capex plus $288B of committed leases. More ATM or hybrid equity, a rating cut toward BBB-/junk risk, and wider project-loan discounts (the landlord loan is already at 89-91c). EPS is ~$8.5-9 and gets 9-10x.

base.story: OCI keeps growing triple digits as GW come online. FY28 revenue lands at ~$125-130B and non-GAAP EPS ~$10-10.5, with continued dilution. FCF stays negative but the FY28 peak-capex message holds, and the multiple stays ~14-15x NTM EPS.

bull.story: Hyperscaler 2027 capex guides come in high and OpenAI's funding (IPO or round) de-risks the backlog. Bring-your-own-hardware and prepaid contracts cut net capex, a positive-FCF path becomes visible in FY29, and margins flatten as management guided. The stock re-rates to ~20x $12+ NTM EPS, still below the peer median.

comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The discount reflects conditions that last through the horizon on management's and consensus's own numbers. (a) Management calls FY27 and FY28 'peak capex years' ($90-95B gross FY27); consensus FCF is -$37B FY27 and -$33B FY28, not positive until FY29. (b) Funding needs equity: a $19.9B ATM in Q1 alone, shares outstanding up to 3.024B. (c) $288B of not-yet-commenced 15-19-year data-center leases, up from $260B a quarter earlier, plus $125B of notes. (d) Backlog concentration: OpenAI anchors a ~$300B contract, and its revenue misses moved ORCL in April. (e) The mix is shifting toward capital-intensive GPU leasing, which the market values at single-digit EBITDA multiples (CRWV 5.9x). None of this relies on sell-side outperform calls.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$98 (~15% under the 52-week low of $114.50 and ~32% below today) the market would be pricing a fundamental break, not volatility. That means a material OpenAI contract deferral or renegotiation, a downgrade toward high yield that forces a halt in funding (equity on dilutive terms, project loans in distress), or a cut to the FY27 revenue guide of at least $90B. At that price the stock implies ~9x CY2027 EPS, which is where my bear case sits.

reasoning: Primary documents first. The Q1 FY27 release and 10-Q (quarter to 2026-08-31) show strong growth: revenue $19.35B +30%, OCI $7.4B +121%, non-GAAP EPS $1.92, RPO $664B (+$26B q/q, >$30B AI bookings) and record OCF of $23.1B. The OCF was flattered by $11.4B of customer prepayments. The funding picture is heavy: capex $28.5B in one quarter (net $18.0B), FCF -$5.4B, a $19.9B ATM equity sale, 3.024B shares, $125B of notes, $288B of not-yet-commenced 15-19-year leases (up from $260B), and the FY26 10-K's $3.3B lessor-loan guarantee no longer mentioned. Management guides FY27 revenue of at least $90B, EPS $8.10, capex $90-95B gross / up to $70B net, calls FY27-28 'peak capex', and gives no date for positive FCF. The standing AI-capex view (Oracle CY27 ~$110B base) is consistent with this. The market has already de-rated ORCL from $322 to $143 (-51% over a year). It trades at 14.6x CY2027 EPS against a peer median of 21.5x on the same basis, and at ~8.7x EBITDA against ~15x. I value it at $154 (P/E $165, SOTP $120, EV/EBITDA $190), only ~7% above spot, because I think a large discount is warranted and will persist. Scenarios are bear $80 (25%), base $155 (50%) and bull $245 (25%), with mean ~$159. The ladder is a lognormal mixture (sigmas 0.32/0.22/0.22), giving an overall spread close to the 56% realized vol. P(>=143) is 0.58, a slight upward tilt from the fair value and positive revision trend (FY28 consensus up from $10.89 to $11.00 over 60 days). The tails stay fat because the binary OpenAI and funding risks are real. Research was limited: SEC blocked scripted access so filings were read via WebFetch, the 10-Q text was truncated (lease figure cross-checked via an independent newsletter), Alpha Vantage was rate-limited and Twelve Data estimates were paywalled.
